To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the observed activity patterns of neurons in visual cortex are a consequence of the connectivity of these neurons and that the activity of the network is a consequence of the activity of the neurons in the preceding layers, and not the other way round.

the anatomically and physiologically measured connection probabilities of a large scale model of primary visual cortex are sufficient to explain the tuning properties of the various neuron populations in the network, and that we introduce a new method to analyze and predict neuronal network responses.

a simple network model of the visual cortex, which just accounts to the anatomically measured connectivity, can explain the firing rates and the orientation selectivity of the neurons in the visual cortex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the understanding of neuronal microcortical function in visual cortex.
understanding the interplay between the connectivity and the algorithm implemented by the neocortex.
the understanding of neuronal microcortical function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the connectivity extracted in anatomical and physiological studies suffices to explain the activity of the various subpopulations in visual cortex.
the network model is able to reproduce the experimental data, but the underlying reasons are still unclear.
the observed activity patterns are the result of a combination of the connectivity structure of the network and the stimulus input.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the connectivity extracted from anatomical and physiological studies is sufficient to explain important properties such as firing rates and orientation preference of different sub populations in visual cortex.
the structure of a network can determine the dynamics of the system.

we show that the structure of neuronal networks can be used to understand the function of these networks, and that this understanding can be used to design experiments that allow for a better understanding of neuronal function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the observed neuronal activity in visual cortex can be explained by the anatomical connectivity of the network.
the connectivity of a neuronal network can be used to predict the emergent activity patterns.
the network structure, which can be extracted from anatomical and physiological data, is already sufficient to predict the emergent activity patterns of neuronal populations.
